g.text: Who you are: the signed anonymous cookie
There is no sign-in. One HttpOnly cookie, signed by the server, is the whole identity.
First visit: the cookie is minted
-> missing, forged or over 30 days old
the page, plus a small client component
whose only job is the call below
mint a random UUID and sign it:
HttpOnly, so no script on the page can read it.
The signature is what makes a user id unforgeable:
the secret never leaves the server.
the browser attaches the cookie by itself
split it, then compare the signature
this visitor's rows and no one else's
[the cookie is more than 30 days old]
Set-Cookie: the same user id, freshly signed
(a returning visitor never loses their history)
treated exactly like a first visit
the response + Set-Cookie for the new id
simply means a new anonymous visitor, who
The trade-off this buys: no passwords, no accounts, no personal data - but clearing
cookies, or switching browser or device, means starting over with an empty history.
